messages:
maya: Heads-up — I want to propose a concrete play for paying down our long-lived tech debt across the inference plane. thinking in terms of debt tranches + recomposition windows.
maya: Goal: reduce cross-service coupling for hotpath requests, shrink runtime HL surface, and make safe rollouts for infra changes.
arjun: +1. can you sketch cadence and deliverables? also who owns the slices?
maya: rough idea: 3 tranches over 6 months. each tranche is 2 months: discover (2w), cut (6w), stabilize (2w). deliverables per tranche: interface contracts, migration adapters, canary runbook, rollback hooks, perf/regression evals.
kim: love the tranche idea. propose we _prioritize_ by coupling score not module size. we should compute a service coupling metric (call graph weight + shared schema churn).
jules: Agree on metrics. suggest we also include runtime-cost impact estimate per tranche so product can fund it.
maya: good call. i'll draft a scoring spreadsheet: coupling, requests/sec on hotpath, token-cost impact estimate, test-coverage delta, risk factor.
samira: For the cut phase: recommend extract-as-a-proxy approach. keep old service behind a thin shim that forwards, with split-traffic config. less blast radius. example:
samira: ```
# shim pseudo-config
route: /v1/generate
backends:
  - id: old-runtime
    weight: 90
  - id: new-runtime
    weight: 10
headers:
  - x-rw-migration: tracer-id
```
samira: we progressively shift weights as confidence improves.
arjun: For interface contracts, prefer a hard typed protobuf for proto-typed internals. don't let JSON shape mutate mid-cut. decouple with an adapter layer so both sides can translate.
kim: add: collect canonical prompt/response pairs for regression tests. store them in the eval harness and gate rollout on quality delta < 1% for core prompts.
jules: Rollout strategy: start with canary on Dedicated instances, shadow traffic in Hosted, then 1% live traffic to tenants with low SLO risk. @ops-bot can we add a checklist to the release-playbook?
ops-bot: deploybot: created checklist "debt-tranche-recomposition-v1" assigned to maya and ops-engineering. link: https://deploy/redwood/checklists/debt-tranche-recomposition-v1
maya: thanks. on ownership — propose pairing one eng lead + one product eng per tranche. product eng owns cost justification and tenant comms.
samira: effort estimates per tranche: discovery 1-2 eng-weeks, cut 6-10 eng-weeks (depending on adapter complexity), stabilize 2-4 eng-weeks. plus SRE ops time for canary and rollback hooks.
arjun: tradeoffs: big-bang extraction reduces duplication but increases rollback complexity. incremental proxy reduces blast radius but increases temporary path complexity and test surface. prefer incremental for infra-facing boundaries.
kim: also need to handle stateful session migration (KV cache ownership). propose we add a compatibility layer to read both old and new caches during cut and reconcile asynchronously.
jules: we should define a short-lived deprecation policy: 3 months post-cut where old path runs in passthrough mode, then scheduled removal if no errors.
maya: Ops/Telemetry: must add request-level tags to measure p50/p95 token-latency, token-cost delta, and error-class. add a tracing flag in shim header: x-rw-migration=true.
samira: quick example of adapter surface we want:
samira: ```
service RuntimeAdapter {
  rpc Generate(GenerateRequest) returns (GenerateResponse);
}
message GenerateRequest {
  string tenant_id = 1;
  bytes prompt = 2;
  int32 max_tokens = 3;
}
```
samira: both old and new adapters implement this shim; adapters own serialization.
arjun: QA: create minimal fuzz harness for corner prompts and a deterministic tokenization test to avoid accidental model drift.
kim: ops note: schedule a trace-day during stabilize for distributed tracing and ingestion retention bump (48h) to allow deep-dive.
jules: product: prepare comms template for tenants (optional migrations notice) and a rollback FAQ.
maya: next actions: 1) I'll open a repo-level RFC with proposed tranche list + scoring sheet. 2) @arjun @kim volunteer to own tranche 1? 3) ops: add checklist entry (done).
arjun: I can co-own tranche 1 (inference-router -> runtime split).
kim: I'll co-own tranche 1 as infra lead.
ops-bot: deploybot: checklist updated: add step "enable x-rw-migration headers".
maya: sweet. i'll post the RFC draft by EOD tomorrow and attach the scoring sheet. any objections?
jules: none from me. :thumbsup:
samira: no objections. start small and measure.
arjun: one more callout — make sure we capture historical perf baselines before any traffic split. snapshotting is cheap and critical.
maya: noted. thanks everyone — we'll sync on Monday at the arch standup for boundary selection.
